purpose: Owner-provided security/process techniques submitted for governed Crucible learning; this manifest is not proof, policy activation, or promotion authority.

techniques.title: Zero-trust custody operations
techniques.threat: A compromised actor or workflow crosses a trust boundary.
techniques.control: Every custody operation must verify exact repository, branch, event, actor and cryptographic identity before mutation.
techniques.verificationPlan: Replay wrong repository, main branch, push event and wrong identity cases; each must fail closed.

techniques.title: Custody micro-segmentation
techniques.threat: A raw, vetted, dashboard or workflow component gains lateral access.
techniques.control: Raw custody, vetted custody, dashboard and workflow identities must remain separate and least-privileged.
techniques.boundary: Crucible custody repositories and Nexus dashboard integration.
techniques.verificationPlan: Attempt cross-repository reads and writes with each identity; every unauthorized edge must fail closed.

techniques.title: One-way evidence boundary
techniques.threat: Telemetry or reports become an inbound mutation path.
techniques.control: Redacted lifecycle evidence may leave the runner, but reports and artifacts cannot write keys, plaintext or custody state back.
techniques.boundary: Key-manager runner report and artifact path.
techniques.verificationPlan: Inspect artifacts and runner cleanup; assert no key material or writable custody path is present.

techniques.title: Encrypted recovery custody
techniques.threat: A compromise or human error destroys the only key or ciphertext state.
techniques.control: Retain encrypted ciphertext and non-secret fingerprints with versioned recovery metadata; never retain plaintext keys.
techniques.boundary: Crucible raw/vetted key lifecycle and recovery records.
techniques.verificationPlan: Restore metadata and ciphertext in a disposable runner; reject missing, mismatched or plaintext recovery inputs.

techniques.title: Endpoint and media control
techniques.threat: Local browser, export or removable media leaks custody material.
techniques.control: The dashboard binds to localhost, requires authentication, never accepts or displays key values, and exports only redacted status.
techniques.verificationPlan: Request unauthenticated, wrong-password and status endpoints; assert no secret fields or browser-wide exposure.

techniques.title: Continuous verification and inhibition
techniques.threat: A stale or altered workflow continues mutating custody.
techniques.control: Exact-head checks, workflow lint, security audits, concurrency and fail-closed provider checks inhibit mutation on drift.
techniques.boundary: Crucible development key manager and governed pipeline.
techniques.verificationPlan: Alter each boundary or remove required authority; the pipeline must stop before secret or custody mutation.

techniques.title: Threat modeling and asset inventory
techniques.threat: Security decisions omit a resource, trust boundary, dependency, or attacker path.
techniques.control: Bind every security change to an explicit asset inventory, threat model, trust boundary, and abuse case before implementation.
techniques.boundary: Crucible repositories, workflows, custody stores, workers, and dashboards.
techniques.verificationPlan: Compare the declared inventory and threat model against the changed paths and reject changes with an uncovered asset or boundary.

techniques.title: Least-privilege authentication and authorization
techniques.threat: A valid identity receives more access than the operation requires.
techniques.control: Use exact repository, branch, event, actor, resource, and operation checks with the smallest available credential scope.
techniques.boundary: Crucible local and hosted workflows plus custody integrations.
techniques.verificationPlan: Replay valid credentials against wrong repositories, branches, events, resources, and operations; each mismatch must fail closed.

techniques.title: Secure software and supply-chain development
techniques.threat: A dependency, build, or release path introduces an exploitable or untraceable change.
techniques.control: Pin actions and dependencies, preserve provenance, review build boundaries, and require reproducible security checks before retention.
techniques.boundary: Crucible source, npm dependencies, GitHub Actions, and release artifacts.
techniques.verificationPlan: Exercise changed dependency, action, lockfile, and artifact paths and require provenance, security, and exact-tip checks.

techniques.title: Audit logging and incident readiness
techniques.threat: A security event cannot be reconstructed, contained, or recovered without destroying evidence.
techniques.control: Retain redacted, integrity-bound audit records, explicit inhibition, bounded response actions, and rollback/recovery custody.
techniques.boundary: Crucible security, custody, workflow, and dashboard operations.
techniques.verificationPlan: Inject representative failures and verify the audit, kill switch, containment, recovery, and rollback chain without secret disclosure.

techniques.title: Vulnerability management feedback
techniques.threat: Known weaknesses recur because findings do not become bounded regression work.
techniques.control: Route findings into candidate experience with exact signatures, affected boundaries, remediation ownership, regression tests, and recurrence review.
techniques.boundary: Crucible security detection, repair, verification, and learning paths.
techniques.verificationPlan: Replay a known finding and a non-reproducing finding; require distinct outcomes and reject unsupported remediation claims.

techniques.title: Application verification and secure authorization flows
techniques.threat: Web or API authorization accepts an untrusted redirect, token, session, or cross-site request.
techniques.control: Verify exact redirect targets, transaction-bound state/nonce, PKCE where applicable, secure token handling, and authenticated service identity.
techniques.boundary: Crucible dashboard, provider integrations, and future Nexus service links.
techniques.verificationPlan: Exercise wrong-origin, replay, open-redirect, missing-state, missing-PKCE, and token-leak cases; all must be refused or contained.

techniques.title: Password-manager-safe human access
techniques.threat: Operators reuse, expose, or lose dashboard credentials during manual intervention.
techniques.control: Use a dedicated password-manager item for the dashboard account, support paste/autofill, require a long unique secret and MFA where available, and never place credential values in source, chat, logs, or learning state.
techniques.boundary: Nexus-hosted Crucible key dashboard and break-glass operator access.
techniques.verificationPlan: Exercise password-manager paste/autofill, wrong-password rate limiting, localhost-only binding, MFA/reauthentication and redacted export; assert no credential value is persisted or returned.

techniques.title: API-key lifecycle and machine identity management
techniques.threat: Long-lived or over-scoped API keys permit unauthorized custody, workflow, or monitoring access.
techniques.control: Use purpose-separated, least-privilege credentials with repository/audience binding, expiration or rotation, dual-key overlap only during governed rotation, revocation, and integrity-bound audit records; prefer GitHub App or OIDC/asymmetric identity where supported.
techniques.boundary: Crucible Actions, key manager, provider integrations, monitoring and custody repositories.
techniques.verificationPlan: Replay expired, revoked, wrong-audience, wrong-repository, over-scoped and rotated credentials; each must fail closed before secret or custody mutation and produce a redacted audit result.

techniques.title: Runtime observability and incident response
techniques.threat: A failure crosses components without enough lineage to diagnose, contain, or roll back it safely.
techniques.control: Propagate a redacted trace identity and exact input/output digests through every boundary; record component, actor, status, failure reason, and rollback reference without storing secrets or executable bytes.
techniques.boundary: Crucible intake, retrieval, extraction, workers, custody, dashboard, diagnostics, and release paths.
techniques.verificationPlan: Inject representative failures and verify one linked trace, exact-tip identity, redacted event lineage, inhibition, and rollback evidence at every boundary.

techniques.title: Distributed and concurrent failure resilience
techniques.threat: Retries, races, restarts, or partial writes duplicate or corrupt candidate and custody state.
techniques.control: Make bounded operations idempotent, use explicit leases and generation checks, and record retry/restart outcomes as candidate evidence rather than silently overwriting state.
techniques.boundary: Crucible queues, workers, publishers, locks, and hosted workflow handoffs.
techniques.verificationPlan: Replay timeout, duplicate delivery, restart, concurrent writer, and partial-publication cases; require deterministic single-outcome state and fail-closed recovery.

techniques.title: Property, contract, and mutation testing
techniques.threat: Example-based tests miss malformed, adversarial, contradictory, or boundary-crossing inputs.
techniques.control: Define invariants for custody, routing, evidence, security, and release boundaries; exercise generated and mutated inputs and retain exact failing seeds and regression results.
techniques.boundary: Crucible validators, evidence packets, routing, retrieval, custody, and release checks.
techniques.verificationPlan: Mutate required fields, hashes, identities, permissions, states, and ordering; every violated invariant must be rejected and every fixed case must have a durable regression.

techniques.title: Secure supply-chain provenance
techniques.threat: A dependency, action, build, or artifact changes without a verifiable origin or review boundary.
techniques.control: Bind dependencies and actions to reviewed versions, capture build and artifact provenance, and require exact-tip security checks before retention or release.
techniques.boundary: Crucible source, npm dependencies, GitHub Actions, hosted runners, and release artifacts.
techniques.verificationPlan: Introduce dependency, action, lockfile, and artifact drift; require provenance mismatch, security failure, or exact-tip mismatch to stop mutation.

techniques.title: Power accountability and human-factors safety
techniques.threat: A highly capable automation path becomes an unchecked authority or suppresses dissent and recovery signals.
techniques.control: Separate evidence production from authorization, preserve dissent and uncertainty, require independent verification and owner approval for promotion, and provide revocation, kill-switch, and rollback paths.
techniques.boundary: Crucible learning, governance, key manager, dashboard, workers, and release paths.
techniques.verificationPlan: Attempt self-approval, verifier conflation, missing dissent, stale authority, and revoked-credential actions; each must fail closed with redacted audit evidence.
